extracted.intended_audience: public relations professionals / PR agencies preparing reports for clients and executives
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for creating monthly public relations coverage reports and templates to communicate campaign performance to clients and executives, including structure, metrics, visuals and forward-looking items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Front-load the report with most valuable insights
rubrics_metrics.description: Front-load the report with the most valuable PR metrics and showcase the best coverage, metrics and activity at the beginning of the report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clients typically have 1-2 minutes of attention to read PR reports, so present key wins and most impactful items first rather than assuming readers will read front-to-back.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide context and explain relevance of results
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain why specific results matter and how they fit into the bigger picture; continually provide context and reinforce objectives for clients or execs who may not fully understand PR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Add context by answering: How does this piece of coverage show we are achieving our objectives? How does this metric demonstrate meaningful progress? How does this activity show we are providing value for money?

rubrics_metrics.name: Include supporting activity and behind-the-scenes work
rubrics_metrics.description: Mention all supporting activities such as PR planning, projects and strategies in the pipeline, and other behind-the-scenes work that contributed to results or is expected to yield results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If there is little coverage for the month, explain what the team is planning and how those activities fit into the overall strategy to justify budgets and show ongoing effort.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on strong visual presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Create a striking visual presentation that conveys a clear message and showcases content in a visual way.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid low-quality screenshots, dense copy and inconsistent formatting. Smart design reflects commitment to delivering results and makes the report easier to absorb.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure what matters — select relevant KPIs
rubrics_metrics.description: Include only the most relevant PR KPIs and break down pivotal metrics rather than overwhelming readers with excessive data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limit to a handful of clear KPIs that matter to the client and their stakeholders; dedicating pages to inconsequential data provides little value and can lessen impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide a table of contents for skimming
rubrics_metrics.description: Add a table of contents so busy clients and executives can quickly identify the most relevant information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A TOC helps readers who cannot read the report front-to-back to navigate directly to key sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Set the scene for the next month — forward-looking statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Include forward-looking statements that explain what is coming next and how ongoing activities build toward broader objectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detail upcoming work to illustrate month-to-month compounding effects of the PR strategy and maintain momentum and alignment among stakeholders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the right format and digital tools
rubrics_metrics.description: Leverage digital reporting tools (rather than static PDFs/Word docs) to present work in an engaging, real-time format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Modern PR activity is better showcased via next-generation reporting tools (e.g., Releasd) that offer visual layouts and real-time data updating; PDF/Word are less engaging.

rubrics_metrics.name: Introduction / Contents section with bullet highlights
rubrics_metrics.description: Start the report with an introduction that outlines completed work and provides a handful of bullet-pointed highlights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many PRs skip this step; a concise intro helps set the scene and primes busy readers for the most important takeaways.

rubrics_metrics.name: Key Metrics section — clear KPIs understandable to stakeholders
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a Key Metrics section with a handful of clear KPIs that are understandable both to the client and their internal stakeholders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: KPIs should be presented in a way that non-PR stakeholders can interpret; avoid technical jargon and explain metrics' significance relative to objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coverage Highlights — showcase most impactful articles upfront
rubrics_metrics.description: If lots of coverage was generated, split out and showcase the most impactful articles and place them near the front of the report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only the most impactful items should be highlighted initially; the remainder of coverage can be shown later in the report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social Wins — include notable social posts with context
rubrics_metrics.description: Include key social media wins and provide context about how social activity fits into the PR strategy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some executives have limited understanding of social's role in PR, so explain why certain social posts matter and how they support wider objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Key Quotes — extract and showcase standout coverage quotes
rubrics_metrics.description: Embed stand-out quotes from coverage and tease out notable lines within the main report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients may not read full articles; pulling key quotes draws attention to earned media value and messaging impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supporting Content — document press releases and collateral
rubrics_metrics.description: Mention supporting content such as press releases, reports, white papers and other collateral that represent valuable behind-the-scenes work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listing supporting content helps justify budgets and demystify the day-to-day work of PR teams.

rubrics_metrics.name: Learnings and Next Steps — quick forward-looking roadmap
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a short section summarizing learnings from the reporting period and clear next steps or upcoming plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A concise 'what's next' maintains momentum, aligns stakeholders, and clarifies how the next period's activities will drive objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be concise and highlight key wins — avoid dense copy
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid dense, wordy paragraphs; make the report scannable and highlight key wins for quick comprehension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dense copy and inconsistent formatting reduce readability; emphasize brevity, bullet points and visual calls-to-action to improve absorption.
